title: Ja'afar the Barmecide and Abd al-Malik

keywords: ja'afar bin yahya and abd al-malik
full_text:
Abd al-Malik, an elderly, respected former governor of Egypt, fell into political disgrace through false court intrigues and had his property confiscated, living in poverty in Baghdad, avoided by all his former colleagues.

Knowing the legendary chivalry of the Barmecide family, Abd al-Malik visited Ja'afar the Barmecide late at night, recounting his unjust humiliation.

Ja'afar did not merely offer him gold. The next morning, during the grand imperial audience of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, Ja'afar took Abd al-Malik by the hand and presented him before the throne.

Ja'afar spoke with magnificent eloquence on Abd al-Malik’s forty years of unblemished service, his honesty in managing the Nile granaries, and the malice of the slanderers who had engineered his fall.

Harun al-Rashid, enlightened by his vizier's courageous defense of an innocent elder, ordered the full restitution of Abd al-Malik’s estates, granted him an imperial pension, and appointed him Counselor of the realm.

Abd al-Malik embraced Ja'afar with tears of gratitude, saying: 'You did not merely save my livelihood, O Barmecide; you restored my honor, which is dearer to me than life itself.'
moral: Generous intercession that restores the honor of a disgraced official earns eternal gratitude.
